questions.question: A caller pretending to be your manager asks for urgent gift cards.
questions.hint: Urgency + pressure = scam.

questions.question: A friend texts from a new number asking for money.
questions.hint: Always verify identity on call.

questions.question: A caller pretends to be your bank manager and demands your ATM PIN urgently.
questions.hint: Banks NEVER ask for PINs.

questions.question: Your boss emails you from an unknown Gmail account asking for vouchers.
questions.hint: Leaders don't use personal emails for urgent money requests.

questions.question: A friend suddenly texts from a new number asking for money without calling.
questions.hint: Always verify identity with a call.

questions.question: A courier calls asking for an OTP to deliver your package.
questions.hint: Couriers never ask for OTPs.

questions.question: A charity worker pressures you to donate immediately at your doorstep.
questions.hint: Pressure = social engineering.

questions.question: An email claims you won a lottery you never entered.
questions.hint: No participation = no prize.

questions.question: Someone you don't know asks for your office WiFi password 'just for one minute'.
questions.hint: Never share network credentials.

questions.question: A stranger on social media asks for your personal number.
questions.hint: Social engineers build trust to steal data.

questions.question: A caller says they're from 'IT support' and wants remote access to your computer.
questions.hint: Remote access requests are suspicious.

questions.question: Someone offers a too-good-to-be-true job if you pay a small 'verification fee'.
questions.hint: Real jobs never charge fees.

questions.question: A coworker asks for your system login because 'his machine isn’t working'.
questions.hint: Credentials should never be shared.

questions.question: An SMS claims to be from your bank but uses a shortened URL.
questions.hint: Short links hide malicious sites.

questions.question: Someone tailgates behind you into an office building claiming their ID card is lost.
questions.hint: Tailgating is a physical social engineering tactic.

questions.question: Your 'bank' asks you to verify account details over a call at odd hours.
questions.hint: Banks follow strict timing and procedures.

questions.question: During onboarding, HR asks for official documents through a verified company portal.
questions.hint: Valid HR processes use secure portals.

questions.question: A stranger claims to be a technician and wants access to your office desk.
questions.hint: Always verify visitor identity.

questions.question: A fake recruiter offers a high salary but asks for your Aadhaar and PAN immediately.
questions.hint: Identity theft risks.

questions.question: A coworker sends a message from an unknown number requesting project files.
questions.hint: Identity must be verified on the official channel.

questions.question: Someone impersonates a courier and asks to sign a digital pad requiring unnecessary details.
questions.hint: Excessive data during delivery = scam.

questions.question: Your electricity provider requests your meter number and account ID via their official app.
questions.hint: Official apps are legitimate channels.

questions.question: A scammer pretends to be your relative stuck in an emergency abroad.
questions.hint: Classic social engineering emotional manipulation.

questions.question: Someone online gains trust over weeks and asks for private photos.
questions.hint: Long-term manipulation is grooming.

questions.question: A fake LinkedIn profile messages you asking for your corporate email.
questions.hint: Attackers use fake profiles to gather credentials.

questions.question: A colleague asks you to open a USB drive found in the parking lot.
questions.hint: USB drops are used for malware attacks.

questions.question: A job application website asks for basic details and clearly states why each one is needed.
questions.hint: Transparency indicates legitimacy.

questions.question: A stranger asks you to forward a confidential company document to help them apply for a job.
questions.hint: Confidential documents must not be shared.

questions.question: You receive a fake tech support popup claiming your system is infected.
questions.hint: Scare tactics drive social engineering scams.

questions.question: A stranger in your office building wears no ID badge but claims to be new.
questions.hint: Unauthorized presence is suspicious.

questions.question: Your bank calls but asks you to provide last 4 digits of your account for confirmation.
questions.hint: Banks may request partial verification data.

questions.question: A scammer pretends to be from customer care and demands remote access to fix an issue.
questions.hint: Remote access = malware risk.

questions.question: A fake government officer demands immediate payment for 'unpaid taxes' and threatens legal action.
questions.hint: Threatening tone = social engineering.

questions.question: Someone claiming to be from your bank says your card is blocked and asks for card details to unblock it.
questions.hint: Banks NEVER ask for card details over call.

questions.question: Your coworker messages from a new WhatsApp number but uses your internal project code names correctly.
questions.hint: Attackers research internal details.

questions.question: A stranger leaves a pen drive on your desk claiming it has 'company guidelines'.
questions.hint: USB drops are common attack vectors.

questions.question: A fake recruiter asks for a video call but tries to convince you to install software first.
questions.hint: Legitimate recruiters don’t require installations.

questions.question: Someone claiming to be a delivery agent asks for your OTP to complete order verification.
questions.hint: OTP should NEVER be shared.

questions.question: An online seller asks you to pay 'half the amount' right now to reserve an item.
questions.hint: Advance payments = risk.

questions.question: A caller pretends to be a government officer and asks for your PAN to confirm 'verification details'.
questions.hint: Govt offices do not verify PAN this way.

questions.question: A well-dressed individual visits your office claiming to be a technician but doesn’t have any ID.
questions.hint: Always insist on identification.

questions.question: A stranger you met online shares a personal story asking for emotional support and money.
questions.hint: Romance scams rely on emotional manipulation.

questions.question: A taxi driver insists on scanning a QR code to confirm your ride.
questions.hint: QR scams can steal money instantly.

questions.question: Someone claiming to be a vendor requests invoice copies through an unofficial email.
questions.hint: Only trust verified vendor domains.

questions.question: A colleague tries to take a photo of your computer screen without asking.
questions.hint: Screens may contain sensitive information.

questions.question: Someone offers you free movie tickets if you fill in your personal data online.
questions.hint: Free offers may collect personal data.

questions.question: You receive a call from 'IT support' asking for your Windows login password.
questions.hint: Support will never ask your password.

questions.question: Someone tailgates behind you into a secure parking area pretending to be an employee.
questions.hint: Unauthorized entry risk.

questions.question: A fake social media page offers free gadgets if you share your ID card photo.
questions.hint: Identity theft risk.

questions.question: Someone from 'customer care' calls and tries to make you download screen-sharing apps.
questions.hint: Screen-sharing = remote control.

questions.question: A stranger on a train tries to view your laptop screen over your shoulder.
questions.hint: Shoulder surfing is a real attack.

questions.question: An acquaintance asks for your personal phone number after just meeting once.
questions.hint: Social engineers collect personal data gradually.

questions.question: You get an email saying your account will be deactivated unless you click an unknown verification link.
questions.hint: Threat tactics are typical in scams.

questions.question: A job consultant asks for an upfront 'resume registration fee'.
questions.hint: Recruitment fees are a scam.

questions.question: An online seller insists you must hurry or lose a 'limited-time offer'.
questions.hint: Urgency tactics manipulate decisions.

questions.question: You notice a coworker rummaging through someone else’s desk without permission.
questions.hint: Unauthorized access = red flag.

questions.question: Someone online asks which school you studied in to 'recover your lost account'.
questions.hint: Attackers collect security question answers.

questions.question: A neighbor requests your WiFi password 'just for a minute'.
questions.hint: Never share your WiFi network.

questions.question: A stranger emails you pretending to be an old friend but lacks personal details.
questions.hint: Impersonation is a social engineering tactic.

questions.question: Someone installs free software on your system without explaining what it does.
questions.hint: Unauthorized installations = threat.

questions.question: A new hire asks you for your login details claiming they 'lost their credentials'.
questions.hint: Credentials must never be shared.

questions.question: A stranger pretends to be a delivery agent and asks to enter your home because 'the package is heavy'.
questions.hint: Attackers use trust to gain physical access.

questions.question: An online marketplace buyer asks you to scan a QR code to receive payment.
questions.hint: QR scams often steal money instead of sending it.

questions.question: A friend sends a link saying 'You need to check this!' without context.
questions.hint: Accounts may be hacked and send malicious links.

questions.question: A visitor claims to be part of a partner company but cannot provide a meeting confirmation.
questions.hint: Social engineers bluff authority.

questions.question: Someone on a video call asks you to tilt your webcam to show your surroundings.
questions.hint: They could be mapping your environment.

questions.question: A person in your building asks to borrow your access card, saying they forgot theirs.
questions.hint: Access cards must never be shared.

questions.question: Someone posing as a charity organizer asks for donations in cash without receipts.
questions.hint: Legitimate charities always provide receipts.

questions.question: You receive a message claiming your package is stuck in customs and requires an urgent small payment.
questions.hint: Money urgency is a scam tactic.

questions.question: An online friend asks for your date of birth to wish you properly.
questions.hint: DOB is used for identity theft.

questions.question: A 'tech support agent' offers to fix your computer for free if you install remote desktop software.
questions.hint: Remote control gives full access to attackers.

questions.question: Attackers impersonate your CEO using a forged email header requesting a confidential report.
questions.hint: CEO fraud emails mimic high-level authority.

questions.question: Someone spoofing your organization's domain sends internal-looking requests for financial transfers.
questions.hint: Domain spoofing is used in advanced scams.

questions.question: A fraudster clones your colleague’s WhatsApp profile picture and name to ask for sensitive documents.
questions.hint: Identity cloning is a high-level social engineering tactic.

questions.question: You receive a forged meeting invite from a real colleague’s email, but the join link redirects to a malicious site.
questions.hint: Attackers use compromised accounts to distribute malware.

questions.question: A cybercriminal calls pretending to be from your IT team using detailed personal information obtained from a data breach.
questions.hint: Breach-based social engineering uses real data to trick victims.

questions.question: An attacker leaves a malicious QR code over an official payment QR at a store.
questions.hint: QR swapping attacks steal funds or data.

questions.question: During a phishing attack, the attacker uses a deepfake voice call to impersonate your manager.
questions.hint: Deepfake voice impersonation is emerging in scams.

questions.question: Someone poses as a telecom engineer and tries to access your roof without appointment, citing a fake work order.
questions.hint: Attackers often fabricate authority with documents.

questions.question: A forged police notice arrives via email demanding your personal details for a 'cybercrime investigation'.
questions.hint: Police never request personal info via email.

questions.question: Attackers create a fake internal helpdesk site identical to your company’s and ask employees to log in.
questions.hint: Credential harvesting via fake portals is advanced phishing.

questions.question: A scammer claims to be from your credit card company and provides the last 4 digits of your card to gain trust.
questions.hint: Partial info does NOT confirm legitimacy.

questions.question: An attacker sends a link saying it's the updated company policy, but the domain uses visually similar characters.
questions.hint: Homoglyph attacks replace letters with lookalikes.

questions.question: A malicious visitor uses fake employee names and meeting titles to gain access to restricted office floors.
questions.hint: Authority impersonation is common in physical SE attacks.

questions.question: Your coworker receives an email appearing to be from your boss but written in unusual language patterns.
questions.hint: Language inconsistency is a clue for impersonation.

questions.question: An attacker sends a deepfake video message requesting confidential internal documents.
questions.hint: Deepfake visual impersonation is used in high-level attacks.

questions.question: A fake auditor visits your company with forged IDs and requests staff details for 'compliance'.
questions.hint: Physical impersonation attacks are sophisticated.

questions.question: An email urges your finance department to urgently change the vendor’s bank account details.
questions.hint: Business Email Compromise targets finance workflows.

questions.question: A scammer uses high-quality forged documents to apply for a loan in your name.
questions.hint: Document forgery is a sophisticated identity-theft tactic.

questions.question: Someone uses social media to gather your birthday, family names, and address for targeted identity attacks.
questions.hint: Oversharing online fuels advanced social engineering.

questions.question: An IT impostor requests admin login credentials claiming ‘system failure risk’.
questions.hint: Attackers escalate urgency to trick targets.

questions.question: Criminals physically impersonate delivery staff to install rogue hardware in office networks.
questions.hint: Hardware implant attacks require strong access control.

questions.question: Attackers create a fake emergency scenario (like a fire drill) to access sensitive rooms during confusion.
questions.hint: Chaos is often used as a distraction.

questions.question: A fraudster uses a spoofed phone number identical to your bank’s number to request verification.
questions.hint: Caller ID spoofing is common in advanced attacks.

questions.question: Someone impersonates your HR department and sends a fake mandatory survey collecting sensitive data.
questions.hint: Internal phishing uses fake HR messages.

questions.question: An attacker uses realistic cloned social media profiles of your coworkers to trick you into sharing internal files.
questions.hint: Cloned profiles are used in advanced social engineering.
